display.purpose: Big Shoulders Display 800, always uppercase at line-height 0.92. Headings, tool names, stamped actions, logotype. Its full stop is a solid square — keep it inside the accent span at hero scale.

body.purpose: Body copy and UI text, sentence case.

label.purpose: 0.6875rem / 600 / 0.16em uppercase. Panel titles, nav, footers, status strips.

force.purpose: JetBrains Mono with tabular figures. Every quantity — bytes, nodes, line and column, tool index. Measurement is always tabular so columns never shift as they update.

motion.name: strike
motion.purpose: The hammer falls: scaleX 0.82 → 1.03 → 1 with a brightness spike. The system's one authored moment, on hero arrival and when an operation lands.

motion.name: draw
motion.purpose: The bar lengthens under the blow — scaleX 0 → 1 from the left.

motion.name: shed
motion.purpose: Scale flecks leaping off the struck end. Decorative only, aria-hidden.

narrative.overview: Stock arrives cold, is brought to heat, struck, measured, and carried out — and it never leaves the shop. That last clause is the product: UtilDock's tools run entirely in the visitor's own tab, and the visual system exists to make that fact physical rather than asserted. The system is built from a working smithy's grammar: a heat scale that reads temperature, stencilled condensed capitals, tabular force numerals, scale-fleck texture, scribed hairlines. Two registers of the same shop, not a theme and its inverse — dark is the forge at heat, light is the cold shop by day, and both are first-class.
keyCharacteristics: Zero border-radius anywhere — struck and stamped, not moulded
Flat: no shadows, depth by tonal layering and rules
One authored motion idea: the strike

rules.name: The Temperature Rule
rules.body: A colour on this site means the work is at a temperature. If a new colour does not report a state, it does not belong in the palette.

rules.name: Three Heat Ramps, Three Jobs
rules.body: Text-safe heat tokens are tuned for contrast and darken in light mode. The billet ramp (--fg-bar-*) is a graphic whose luminance must climb to the hot end in both registers. Stamp tokens are identical in both registers because the metal is hot in both. Never draw the bar from the text tokens, and never stamp onto it with theme-following colours.

rules.name: Measurement Is Tabular
rules.body: Every figure that is a quantity uses .ud-force — mono with tabular-nums — so columns align and never shift as values update.

rules.name: The World Recedes On Tools
rules.body: Landing is Persuade, tool pages are Operate, prose pages are Read. On a tool page expression may never obscure the task, its state, or a familiar affordance. Reading pages return h2/h3 to sentence-case Archivo via .ud-prose.

rules.name: Same-Origin Or Not At All
rules.body: public/_headers ships a CSP with default-src 'self' and connect-src 'self' and no 'unsafe-eval'. Fonts, images and scripts are self-hosted; a library that compiles code at runtime cannot be used. This is the mechanism behind the product's privacy claim, not a preference.

dos: Do treat colour as temperature — a new colour must report a state
Do keep every figure in .ud-force with tabular figures
Do self-host any new font, image or script
Do verify contrast in both registers; small legend text is the usual casualty
Do let side-by-side panels share row tracks with the `aligned` prop
donts: Don't add a border-radius, drop shadow, glass, or any gradient that isn't the billet
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading
Don't use a library that compiles code at runtime — the CSP omits 'unsafe-eval'
Don't rebuild the tool directory as a card grid
Don't scatter animation; the system has one authored moment, and all of it collapses under prefers-reduced-motion
